newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian PM nominee says king's stand premature.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian PM nominee says king's stand premature.

text.p: Cambodian Foreign Minister Ung Huot said on Tuesday that King Norodom Sihanouk's refusal to recognise his nomination as first prime minister was premature because the nation's parliament had yet to decide on the issue.
Sihanouk said on Monday that he would not recognise Ung Huot as first prime minister as the position belonged to his son, Prince Norodom Ranariddh.
"How can he say that if the National Assembly has not made a decision yet," Ung Huot told reporters.
"Whatever people do here it should be credible and legal," he said without elaborating.

Ung Huot, a senior member of Ranariddh's FUNCINPEC party, was nominated to replace Ranariddh by party members who remained in Cambodia after the prince's overthrow by Second Prime Minister Hun Sen on July 6.

Hun Sen backs Ung Huot's nomination to replace Ranariddh, but the prince, in his capacity as president of FUNCINPEC, expelled Ung Huot from the party on the weekend. Ung Huot dismissed the move as an act of desperation and a joke.

Sihanouk said in comments faxed to news agencies in Beijing on Monday that Ranariddh had the right to retain the title of first prime minister unless he was formally condemned by an independent Cambodian tribunal.
"While maintaining my affection for him, I will abstain from giving His Excellency Mr Ung Huot his new title of 'first prime minister'," Sihanouk said.

Ranariddh left Cambodia on the eve of fighting in the capital that led to his overthrow. Hun Sen later said the prince could return to Cambodia, but he would have to face trial for alleged illegal negotiations with the outlawed Khmer Rouge guerrilla group and for alleged weapons smuggling.

Many FUNCINPEC members and supporters fled the country following Ranariddh's overthrow and the subsequent crackdown on his supporters in which some 40 people were killed, according to human rights investigators.
About 20 members of FUNCINPEC and a small allied party were absent when the 120-member National Assembly was convened on Monday.
Sihanouk said Ung Huot's appointment by an incomplete parliament would be invalid.

"The decisions of an incomplete parliament working under conditions of very questionable 'freedom' and 'regularity' could not be considered valid within the spirit of our 1993 Constitution and our liberal democracy," he said.
Meanwhile, National Assembly President Chea Sim on Monday called for Ung Huot to be approved as first prime minister in place of Ranariddh.
Cambodian assembly officials said administrative delays meant voting on Ung Huot's nomination might be delayed until next week.

Ranariddh arrived in Beijing on Friday for what officials insist is a private visit with his father, who is receiving medical treatment there. The king maintains a palatial residence in the Chinese capital.
In his faxed comments, Sihanouk said he was still too ill to return to his troubled Southeast Asian homeland.
In an apparent recognition of Hun Sen's political grip on Cambodia, Sihanouk stressed he would not oppose laws passed since the second prime minister seized control.
